title: Product protocol computes componentwise
statement:
Let $p_1$ be a finite-message protocol with input types $X_1$, $Y_1$ and output type $\alpha_1$, and let $p_2$ be a finite-message protocol with input types $X_2$, $Y_2$ and output type $\alpha_2$. For every pair of inputs $x = (x_1, x_2) \in X_1 \times X_2$ and $y = (y_1, y_2) \in Y_1 \times Y_2$, running the product protocol of $p_1$ and $p_2$ on $(x, y)$ yields the pair of the two componentwise executions:
\[
  \mathrm{run}(p_1 \times p_2,\, x,\, y) \;=\; \bigl(\mathrm{run}(p_1,\, x_1,\, y_1),\; \mathrm{run}(p_2,\, x_2,\, y_2)\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: p_1 a finite-message protocol over (X_1, Y_1, alpha_1)
p_2 a finite-message protocol over (X_2, Y_2, alpha_2)
input x = (x_1, x_2) in X_1 x X_2
input y = (y_1, y_2) in Y_1 x Y_2
replaced:
For protocols $p_1$, $p_2$ and inputs $x = (x_1, x_2)$, $y = (y_1, y_2)$,
\[
  (p_1.\texttt{prod}\;p_2).\texttt{run}\;x\;y
  \;=\; (p_1.\texttt{run}\;x_1\;y_1,\; p_2.\texttt{run}\;x_2\;y_2).
\]
